content: The hum of the servers was a lullaby for the broken, a white noise symphony masking the footsteps of the man in the trenches of the data center. His trench coat, a relic of a time before bytes and firewalls, brushed against the cold metal racks as he flicked a cigarette butt to the concrete floor, its ember dying like a last hope. The flickering fluorescent lights cast long shadows on the rows of blinking machines, each one a silent witness to the secrets they held. He was here for a data heist, a job that smelled of desperation and cheap cologne. The air was thick with the scent of ozone and betrayal, and the only sound was the steady hum of the machines, indifferent to the fate of the man who dared to steal their secrets.
